mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% and 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with a slowing economy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5pp and 5-day forward returns are positive in > 70% of triggered instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines for 2 consecutive months and 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases > 1% MoM and 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, it signals a tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL is increasing, yet 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of triggered instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with strong job growth
failure_condition: If UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000, yet 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases for 3 consecutive months and 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) is above its 12-month moving average and the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3%, it signals a supply-side expansion with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO > 12-month MA and FEDFUNDS < 3%, yet 60-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of triggered instances, or if Rank IC < 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.
